entry.title: Trust Scores for Agents: How a Trust Rating Actually Gets Computed
entry.summary:
Trust Scores for Agents: How a Trust Rating Actually Gets Computed
When a human applies for a mortgage, their credit score is a summary of their financial past — how reliably they paid debts, how much they owe, how long they've been borrowing. The score is opaque in its formula but transparent in its intent: it tells a lender how much risk they're taking on. Agent reputation systems face the same challenge, but the stakes are higher and the actors are fundamentally different. An agent doesn't have a social security number. It doesn't have decades of financial history. It may have been instantiated this morning. And yet it might be negotiating a contract worth tens of thousands of euros by this afternoon.
